sources.title: Nationaal Archief, Soevereiniteitsoverdracht Indonesië (1949)
sources.note: Original national archive exhibit directly read, proclamation, colonial war, federal settlement and 27 December 1949 transfer. Its occupation starting-year shorthand is not repeated.

sources.title: Congressional Research Service, Indonesia: Domestic Politics, Strategic Dynamics, and U.S. Interests (31 January 2011)
sources.note: Original PDF directly read, printed pages 6 to 8 and 30. Used for historical government transitions only, not 2011 demographics or officeholders presented as current.

sources.title: National Security Archive, U.S. Embassy Tracked Indonesia Mass Murder 1965 (2017)
sources.note: Original archival exhibit and documentary description read. Army and paramilitary mass murder of alleged PKI supporters in 1965 to 1966, imprisonment and Suharto transition. No disputed precise death toll asserted.

sources.title: UNESCO, Asian-African Conference Archives
sources.note: Original registration entry read. Bandung, 18 to 24 April 1955, 29 countries, anti-colonial cooperation and surviving documents, pictures and films.

sources.title: United Nations, UNSF: Background
sources.note: Original mission history read: UNTEA administration 1962 to 1963 and administrative transfer on 1 May 1963. Does not establish universal consent or resolve ongoing political disputes.

sources.title: United Nations, UNMISET: Background
sources.note: Original mission account indexed text read; 1999 consultation and violence, UN transitional administration, independence May 2002. Separate Timor-Leste state not merged with Indonesia.

sources.title: World Bank, Making the New Indonesia Work for the Poor (2006)
sources.note: Original indexed Chapter 2 read: financial crisis, 1998 political change, decentralization laws effective in 2001. No old poverty measures reused as current.

sources.title: World Bank, Community Driven Development in Indonesia (1 August 2014)
sources.note: Original project account directly read. KDP began 1998, PNPM Mandiri launched 2007, community planning, employment and small-scale infrastructure.

sources.title: UNESCO, Indonesian Batik (2009 inscription)
sources.note: Original indexed element text read; direct HTML challenge. Wax-resist dyeing, repeated colours, life-cycle uses. The same element is also served at /indonesian-batik-00170; both one work.

sources.title: Meghan Hynson, Indonesian Angklung: Intersections of Music Education and Cultural Diplomacy, Smithsonian
sources.note: Original museum scholarly essay directly read. Single-tone bamboo instruments, ensemble cooperation, educational use and cultural diplomacy. Archived article-hynson.php is same work.

sources.title: UNESCO, Jamu wellness culture (2023 inscription)
sources.note: Original element text directly read: mostly adult women makers, herbs and spices, cultivation, family/neighbour transmission and customer trust. Used for cultural practice, not efficacy or treatment recommendations.

sources.title: UNICEF, Be grateful for every penny: Marlina’s story (21 December 2020)
sources.note: Original profile read: Sabang mother, cake orders/laundry and injured fisherman husband during COVID-19; GEUNASEH support, eggs/fish/vegetables and posyandu counselling. Same story reprinted in 2021 One Year On report; count as one work.

sources.title: UNICEF, Building Better Foundations for Young Learners in West Papua (30 December 2025)
sources.note: Original directly read. Teacher Bertha, Gracia, Sinar Hungku centre; high-fives, shortages, weather, children accompanying parents to fields. Named local case, not generalization about all Papuan schools.

sources.title: UNICEF, On the way to healthier communities with WASH FIT (20 February 2024)
sources.note: Original directly read. Nur Annisa, age 18, Puskesmas Mancobalang, Gowa, South Sulawesi; accessible and gender-separated toilets, menstrual kits, mirrors, solar panels and water towers. Healthcare facility, not school installation.

sources.title: World Mosquito Program, Wolbachia dramatically reduces dengue cases (June 2021)
sources.note: Original trial-team release directly read. AWED randomized trial, Gadjah Mada/Monash/Tahija, 24 clusters, 77% dengue reduction and 86% hospitalization reduction, routine control in both groups. Same underlying NEJM trial across reports and translations.

sources.title: Miklos Gaspar, Twenty years on: Indonesia’s disaster preparedness, UN Indonesia (2024)
sources.note: Original UNIC field report indexed text read, first published UN News 11 October 2024. Simeulue smong oral tradition, 1907 memory, 2004 survival and school teaching. No inconsistent precise island death count repeated.

sources.title: UNESCO, Borobudur Temple Compounds
sources.note: Original entry directly read, Authenticity: 1973 to 1983 restoration, mostly original stones and added drainage. Prior Mataram runtime reuse must be included. Modern conservation distinguished from eighth/ninth-century construction.

sources.title: Arsip Nasional Republik Indonesia, Majalah ARSIP, edition 61 (2013)
sources.note: Original 58-page PDF directly read. PDF page 6, lines 259 to 261, gives proclamation opening in modern spelling. Original historical spelling differs; public label expressly modernized transcription. Literal English translation supplied, no facsimile claim.

sources.title: Congressional Research Service, U.S.-Indonesia Relations, IF10247 (5 June 2025)
sources.note: Original official HTML directly read, Political Background and democracy/institutions; dated contemporary context. No current officeholder statement or election turnout statistic used.

sources.title: MPR legal archive, Decree XLIV/MPRS/1968: appointment as President
sources.note: Original legal catalogue indexed text checked. 1968 presidential appointment; distinct from acting presidency in 1967 and earlier consolidation of power. Used only for the formal phase boundary.

proposedOverrides.name: Indonesia
proposedOverrides.summary: Indonesia’s modern republic grew from the 1945 independence struggle and changed through authoritarian rule and democratic reform.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Exact ID only, no aliases associated. Earlier kingdoms and colonial records are distinct; Timor-Leste remains separate.
batchIdentityNotes.geometry: 1945 features span [95.19,-10.378,130.806,5.57], with a separate Bangka-area polygon [105.198,-3.175,106.642,-1.627]. From world-1960 onward the main feature reaches 140.961E, including western New Guinea before the actual administrative transfer on 1 May 1963. Public dated warning retained. Bbox alone does not establish precise Timor inclusion or sovereignty.
batchIdentityNotes.interval: 1945 to present, final period exclusive 2027 displays examples through 2026 and is not a fall prediction.
batchIdentityNotes.sourceWorkGroups: Batik URL variants one work; Wolbachia trial mirrors/translations one work; Marlina profile and annual-report reprint one work. Borobudur runtime Mataram reuse must be charged.
batchIdentityNotes.writing: Modern-spelling archive transcription of a genuine 1945 declaration, original Latin script; literal translation supplied. No separate transliteration needed.
